respuesta.pregunta: In catalog-portfolio-api 0.0.1-test-bench-v2a, what states can a brand go through, and which endpoint do I call to take an ACTIVE brand back to STAND_BY?
respuesta.respuesta:
The brand management guide lists three states [catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/brand-management/README.md:L71-L71]:

- **STAND_BY**: the brand exists but isn't active yet. It may be missing required logos, or it may have been temporarily deactivated [catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/brand-management/README.md:L105-L105].
- **ACTIVE**: the brand is fully functional and visible, and all requirements are met [catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/brand-management/README.md:L106-L106].
- **DELETED**: the brand has been permanently removed, and this can't be undone [catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/brand-management/README.md:L107-L107].

According to the state diagram, a new brand starts in STAND_BY. From STAND_BY it can go to ACTIVE, and from ACTIVE it can go back to STAND_BY. A brand in either state can move to DELETED [catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/brand-management/README.md:L88-L92].

The docs only name an endpoint for the STAND_BY → ACTIVE step: `PUT /catalog/brands/{brandId}/activate` [catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/api-reference/README.md:L30-L30]. Deletion uses `DELETE /catalog/brands/{brandId}` [catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/api-reference/README.md:L29-L29].

I can't say which endpoint takes an ACTIVE brand back to STAND_BY. The diagram shows that transition, but none of the documentation I have names an endpoint or operation for it. That doesn't mean no such operation exists. It just isn't described here.
answer_checks: Lists the three brand states STAND_BY, ACTIVE and DELETED, with citations to the brand management guide.
Describes the documented transitions, including that a new brand starts in STAND_BY and that ACTIVE can go back to STAND_BY.
States that no endpoint or operation for the ACTIVE → STAND_BY transition is documented.
Does not make up a deactivation endpoint (e.g. a /deactivate route) or say that deactivating through PUT update is supported.
Does not claim that deactivation is unsupported or impossible; it only says it is undocumented.
